To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the division number dependent proliferation and death rates are the main characteristics of the CFSE proliferation assay and the information-theoretically based method is the best approach to estimate the model parameters and evaluate the goodness of fit of the mathematical model.
the lymphocyte death rate is dependent upon the number of divisions and the death rate is higher for cells that have undergone a larger number of divisions.

(1) the proliferation of T lymphocytes in vitro and in the mouse model in vivo are both division number dependent; (2) the heterogeneity of cell kinetics should be incorporated into the structure and parameters of mathematical models; (3) the maximum likelihood method is the most robust and computationally efficient technique for parameter estimation; and (4) the profile-likelihood method is a useful tool for evaluating parameter identifiability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of computational tools for the analysis of CFSE data and the application of these tools to the analysis of the data obtained in the course of a lymphocyte proliferation assay.
the development of a mathematical model of cell proliferation and its application to the analysis of experimental data on the proliferation of T lymphocytes in vitro.
the development of computational tools for the analysis of CFSE data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heterogenous linear model is the best model for describing the kinetics of PHAdriven human T lymphocyte CFSE proliferation.

the mathematical models of cell proliferation and cell death should be based on a heterogenous compartmental structure and should incorporate division number-dependent rates, which are not necessarily linear.
the heterogenous compartmental model provides a good description of the experimental CFSE data and is a useful tool in the analysis of cell kinetics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heterogeneity of lymphocyte proliferation and cell death is the key factor in the development of the mathematical model for the CFSE assay.
the CFSE data can be successfully analyzed using mathematical modelling and the maximum likelihood method.
the mathematical model we propose is able to capture the essential characteristics of the CFSE data and the parameter estimation techniques are capable of providing reliable parameter estimates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the information-theoretically based approach is the most reliable and robust for parameter estimation and model selection.

the information-theoretically based approach to model selection and parameter estimation can be used to identify the most appropriate mathematical model of cell proliferation and to obtain the best possible estimates for the model parameters.
the CFSE data analysis should be done using a model-based approach, which is the only way to obtain reliable estimates of the model parameters.
